issues.legal_issue: An assignee cannot enforce a contractual purchase right that the assignor waived with the other parties’ consent.
material_facts: The original buyer’s heirs and the estate’s surviving family members executed a lease and a later sale agreement in favour of another purchaser, with the stated intention of facilitating completion of the original sale transaction.

The assignee’s pleadings accepted that the later documents were obtained to support closing the original transaction, and the assignor’s consent to those documents was inferred from the parties’ pleadings and conduct.
The assignor and the assignee did not give evidence at trial.
issues.conclusion: The original buyer had waived his right to purchase the estate, so the assignee acquired no better right and could not enforce the agreement for specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: Waiver is an agreement to release or not assert a right. Under Satyanarayana v. Yellogi Rao (1965) 2 SCR 222, once waiver is established, no question of judicial discretion arises; waiver may be inferred from conduct and the circumstances. An assignee cannot obtain a greater right than the assignor possessed.

predicates.appeal_from_specific_performance_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree granting specific performance.
predicates.assignor_consented_to_substitute_transac: The original holder of the contractual right consented to a later transaction concerning the same property.
predicates.substitute_transaction_intended_to_settl: The parties intended the later transaction to facilitate or settle the original contractual arrangement.
predicates.assignee_cannot_enforce_waived_right: The assignee cannot enforce a contractual right that the assignor waived.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a specific-performance decree concerns a right that its holder consented to settle through a substitute transaction, the assignee cannot enforce that waived right.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance is not automatic merely because it is lawful, and the court may refuse it where the suit’s motive and circumstances show that the remedy would be used oppressively to obtain an unfair advantage.
material_facts: The suit for specific performance was brought after the intended purchaser under the later transaction failed to obtain the estate and the purchaser who obtained the conveyance was unwilling to give it up.
The original contractual right relied on in the suit had been waived, and the claimant relied on an assignment of that right.
The purchaser in possession had obtained the conveyance and made substantial improvements to the estate.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to specific performance; the decree granting it was reversed and the trial court’s judgment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 preserves judicial discretion over specific performance. A court must consider all facts and circumstances, including the motive behind the litigation, and must guard against using the remedy as an instrument of oppression or to secure an unfair advantage. Specific performance is not required merely because it is lawful to grant it.

predicates.appeal_from_specific_performance_decree: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree granting specific performance.
predicates.claim_based_on_waived_right: The claimant seeks to enforce a contractual right that the original holder waived.
predicates.suit_motive_is_to_gain_unfair_advantage: The suit was brought to obtain an advantage over a person who acquired and retained the property after another intended purchaser failed to obtain it.
predicates.specific_performance_must_be_refused: The court refuses to grant specific performance.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a specific-performance decree, the court refuses the remedy when the claim rests on a waived right or the suit is motivated by obtaining an unfair advantage.
